translation.name: Bogotá
translation.summary: Colombia’s capital combines the historic La Candelaria district, the Gold Museum, views from Monserrate and colourful street art with modern architecture.

translation.body:
Bogotá is Colombia’s capital and largest city, where colonial architecture, contemporary towers, steep streets and lively neighbourhoods meet. Begin in La Candelaria, the old city district, with its preserved historic buildings and churches.

The Church of Santa Clara is known for its decorative painting, while San Ignacio is another historic landmark. Colombia’s pre-Columbian heritage can be explored at the Gold Museum and the National Museum. Monserrate rises above the city and offers wide views over Bogotá; the Botanical Garden provides a different perspective on the region’s plants.

Museums are a major attraction, from the Gold Museum and exhibitions of emeralds to archaeology, religious art, numismatics and the collections associated with notable Colombians. The city also has museums and memorials linked to Simón Bolívar and Gabriel García Márquez.

Street art, parks, colonial façades and newer districts all contribute to Bogotá’s distinctive city life. Ada Tours can combine a city excursion with visits to Monserrate and museums before the journey continues elsewhere in Colombia.
